finding: The 350 MHz and 400 MHz Pentium II records are separately named speed grades in the same introduction and are not duplicate identities.

recommended_next_action: Retain both frozen speed-grade records; only part-number evidence could justify a finer SKU split.

finding: Plain 300 MHz Celeron and 300A MHz Celeron are distinct manufacturer designations and cannot be collapsed by numeric speed.
source_evidence: Intel describes 300A MHz as a new cached Celeron while describing 300 MHz as a separate offered speed without integrated L2 cache.
recommended_next_action: Preserve both keys and raw names; obtain orderable identifiers before making a SKU-level claim.

finding: The 233 MHz and 266 MHz mobile Pentium II entries are separate named speed variants introduced together; shared announcement timing is not duplicate identity.
source_evidence: Intel names both speeds and gives separate mini-cartridge and mobile-module availability details.
recommended_next_action: Retain two speed-grade records and keep their shared date as independently stated rather than inherited from a family record.

finding: The two frozen OverDrive output-speed keys describe one singular Pentium II OverDrive product with two compatibility/output mappings rather than independently evidenced physical products.
source_evidence: Intel uses singular product wording and one MSRP while mapping two Pentium Pro input groups to 300 MHz and 333 MHz outputs.
recommended_next_action: Require a human merge-or-restructure decision: preserve both frozen records as provenance but model one product plus compatibility assertions unless part-number evidence supports separate products.

finding: The AMD-K6-2 family and four speed-grade records intentionally overlap across granularities; the family must not be counted as a fifth speed-grade record or used to infer an exhaustive launch-SKU list.
source_evidence: AMD states a May 28 family introduction and quarterly shipment totals but does not enumerate the family launch speed grades.
recommended_next_action: Retain the family as a family-level candidate and each speed grade only as separately evidenced variants; do not use the group as a count of five comparable SKU claims.

finding: The exact May 28 AMD-K6-2 family date cannot be inherited by any speed-grade candidate. The 350 MHz variant is Q3 evidence and the 366 MHz 380 MHz and 400 MHz variants are Q4 evidence only.
source_evidence: AMD's Q4 filing identifies 366 MHz 380 MHz and 400 MHz versions as introduced and shipped in volume during Q4; it does not supply an exact date.
recommended_next_action: Keep the family exact date and each speed-grade interval separately typed; reject any normalization that converts quarter evidence to day or month precision.

finding: All four AMD-K6-2 speed-grade timing claims are manufacturer-controlled retrospective quarter statements. They support bounded 1998 intervals but not exact first-shipment dates or orderable identities.
source_evidence: The Q3 filing supports the 350 MHz interval while the Q4 filing supports 366 MHz 380 MHz and 400 MHz intervals; neither resolves exact dates.
recommended_next_action: Retain quarter precision and flag independent contemporary or channel evidence as optional follow-up rather than filling missing dates.

finding: The Xeon 400 MHz record has a cache-configuration boundary: Intel names 512 KB and 1 MB L2 options with different prices and later boxed-channel timing. A single record must not imply a fully resolved single SKU.
source_evidence: Intel gives separate cache-option pricing and distinguishes June 29 component availability from later boxed availability.
recommended_next_action: Keep the record at unresolved model-variant granularity until human review chooses whether cache configurations require separate candidate or assertion treatment.

finding: Xeon 450 has an exact October 6 announcement but only planned two-way system shipments later in October; four-way availability is stated for early 1999. Announcement and planned shipment must not be converted into completed 1998 commercial availability.
source_evidence: Intel calls the event an announcement and distinguishes planned two-way system shipments from early-1999 four-way availability.
recommended_next_action: Keep the record review-required until a human chooses whether announcement plus planned 1998 system shipment meets the cohort event rule or later evidence establishes a completed qualifying event.

finding: The mobile 300 MHz AMD-K6 record is not documented as an AMD-K6-2 speed variant. Its mobile AMD-K6 wording must remain separate from the AMD-K6-2 family and speed-grade hierarchy.
source_evidence: AMD states that it introduced a 300 MHz AMD-K6 processor for mobile applications during Q3 without calling it AMD-K6-2.
recommended_next_action: Do not assign AMD-K6-2 parentage or May family timing to the mobile AMD-K6 record; retain a separate family/category label pending product-identity evidence.

finding: The expanded run now covers every Intel item listed in the frozen 1998 Intel chronological register plus the OverDrive upgrade product. That does not establish a complete Intel-and-AMD market cohort because the AMD source set is not a chronological product register and no shared manufacturer or segment stopping rule is declared.

recommended_next_action: State the intended manufacturer and segment stopping rule before declaring cohort completeness; do not manufacture additional AMD product keys from family shipment totals.

finding: The expanded cohort spans component introductions; system availability; boxed channels; mobile OEM modules; upgrade reseller availability; and planned system shipments. These are legitimate segment-specific facts but no single availability event can be assumed equivalent across all records.

recommended_next_action: Maintain typed event and channel fields through human review; do not rank or filter records by a single unqualified release-date column.
